post.description: Generates a model response for a chat conversation. OpenAI-compatible — set your OpenAI SDK's base URL to `{app}/api/v1` and use your API key. Set `stream: true` for a Server-Sent Events stream of `chat.completion.chunk` objects ending with `[DONE]` (the chunk before it carries `usage` when the model reports its token counts). Billed per token (prompt + completion).

200.description: The completion: one choice holding the assistant's message, and `usage` counting the tokens billed. With `stream: true`, the completion comes as Server-Sent Events instead (`text/event-stream`).

schema.description:
Sent instead of the JSON when `stream: true`. Each event is a `data: ` line holding one JSON object, then a blank line:

1. A `chat.completion.chunk` whose `choices[0].delta` is `{"role": "assistant"}`.
2. One chunk for each piece of the answer, with the text in `choices[0].delta.content`. `finish_reason` is `null` until the chunk that ends the answer, which names it; that chunk may have an empty `delta`.
3. When the model reports its token counts, one more chunk with `choices: []` and `usage` (`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`).
4. Last, always: `data: [DONE]`, which is not JSON.

Every chunk repeats the same `id`, `created` and `model`. If the model fails once the stream has started, the status stays 200: one event holding the error envelope, with the code `upstream_error`, takes the place of the chunks still to come and of the `usage` chunk, and `data: [DONE]` follows. The prompt and the text already sent are billed, from estimated token counts.

X-Cost.description: The price billed, in credits. Sent with the JSON completion; a stream is billed when it ends, so it carries none.

X-Accel-Buffering.description: Sent as `no` with a stream: it tells a proxy such as nginx not to hold back the events.

post.description:
Synthesizes speech from text and answers with WAV audio. Pass `voice_id` to use a stock voice or one of your voice clones.

Optional `quality` selects a latency/fidelity preset: `fast` (lowest latency, slightly reduced detail), `standard` (default, balanced), `high` (best fidelity, slowest).

Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe: replaying the same key returns the original audio and headers instead of synthesizing and charging again. Keys are scoped to your organization, must not exceed 191 characters (a longer key answers 400 `invalid_request` before anything is synthesized or charged), and are remembered for 7 days. The same key sent with a different body answers 409 `idempotency_conflict`.

The response carries the price billed (`X-Cost`), billed character count (`X-Character-Count`), your balance after the charge (`X-Balance`), voice type (`X-Voice-Custom`), upstream latency (`X-Latency-Ms`) and a request id (`X-Request-Id`) in headers. A response replayed from an `Idempotency-Key` also carries `Idempotency-Replayed: 1`.

Emotion tags are bracketed directions the voice acts out rather than reads aloud: `[laughter]`, `[sigh]`, `[dissatisfaction-hnn]`, `[confirmation-en]`, `[question-en]`, `[question-ah]`, `[question-oh]`, `[question-ei]`, `[question-yi]`, `[surprise-ah]`, `[surprise-oh]`, `[surprise-wa]`, `[surprise-yo]`. Write them inline in the text. Each bills as one character rather than as its spelling, so a tag costs the same however long its name is.

post.description:
Renders a multi-speaker script into one stitched WAV file. `turns` holds 1–100 entries, each with a `voice_id` (a stock voice or one of your clones) and its `text`, and optionally its own `language`, `quality` and `speed`; `gap_ms` (0–5000) sets the silence between turns. Billed per character, per turn, at that turn's own rate.

Over 8000 characters in total answers 413 `input_too_large`; a single turn over its own limit answers 422 `invalid_request`.

The response carries `X-Cost`, `X-Balance`, `X-Character-Count`, `X-Voice-Custom`, `X-Latency-Ms` and `X-Request-Id`, as synthesize does. It adds per-turn start and end offsets in `X-Turns` (a JSON array with snake_case keys) and the number of turns in `X-Turn-Count`, so a client can seek to a line. `Idempotency-Key` works as on synthesize.

Emotion tags are bracketed directions the voice acts out rather than reads aloud: `[laughter]`, `[sigh]`, `[dissatisfaction-hnn]`, `[confirmation-en]`, `[question-en]`, `[question-ah]`, `[question-oh]`, `[question-ei]`, `[question-yi]`, `[surprise-ah]`, `[surprise-oh]`, `[surprise-wa]`, `[surprise-yo]`. Write them inline in the text. Each bills as one character rather than as its spelling, so a tag costs the same however long its name is.

An explicit `null` clears `tags` or `ref_text`; `tags: []` clears the tags and `ref_text: ""` clears the transcript. Blank tags are dropped. The clone keeps its `id`, so existing `voice_id` references keep working.

Changing the language or the transcript re-creates the voice on the voice service. Whenever the voice service fails, the answer is 502 `upstream_error` with a message written for people, such as "The voice service is temporarily unavailable." when it cannot be reached, or "Voice update failed. Please try again later." when a rename or retag is refused, which changes nothing. Match on the status and `code`, not on the message. When re-creating fails after the old voice was removed, the previous version is put back where possible, and the message says whether it was. If the service has lost the voice's sample, a change that re-creates it answers "The current sample is no longer available. Upload a new one to save these changes.": upload a new clip with POST /api/v1/tts/voices/{id}/audio first.

post.description:
Creates a key. `name` (1–80 characters) and `access` (`full` or `restricted`) are required. A restricted key holds exactly the levels in `permissions`; a full key holds every product, and its `permissions` may then name only `api_keys`. `allowed_ips` is a list of addresses or CIDR ranges, and `monthly_spend_limit` is in credits per calendar month (UTC).

Answers 201 with the key and its `secret`. This is the only time the secret is ever shown, so store it now.

The new key never holds more than the calling key. A restricted caller cannot create full keys or set a product above its own level, and the caller's own `api_keys` level caps the one it grants. The new key cannot have looser limits either: if the caller expires, the new key must expire no later; if the caller has a monthly spend limit, the new key needs one no higher; and if the caller has an IP allowlist, every entry of the new key's must appear in the caller's, compared entry by entry. A violation answers 403 `insufficient_permissions`.

A spend limit applies to each key on its own. A key made through the API outlives the key that made it, and per-key rate and concurrency overrides are not inherited.

Cache-Control.description: Includes `no-store`: the answer holds the new key's secret, so no cache may keep a copy.
